names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 27 iunie, «Sfânta Ioana Mironosița»; the form is the bare name, «Mironosița» being the title the calendar gives her, the myrrhbearer.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 27 Ιουνίου, «Αγία Ιωάννα η Μυροφόρος», with the rank word and the epithet left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 27. јун ст. ст., „Света Јоана Мироносица“ — Света is not a rank and Мироносица is the rank, which §6 takes off and which this corpus has no type for, as the row records. The bare forename is what is left, and the «wife of Chuza» of the display name is the corpus’s own, off the body of this entry and of the other two books’ lines, and §10 reserves it. **The spelling is this book’s own and is copied as printed**: it writes Јоана with one н, where the Romanian form on this folder is «Ioana» and the Greek «Ιωάννα» with two; nothing is regularised and nothing is transliterated. `foldchk.py` returns NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM and `.tmp/sr-foldpred.mjs` returns no other holder of the gate’s folded key, **which is worth the line on a name this common**: the corpus keeps dozens of Johns and this is its first Serbian Joanna, so no `READ_FOLDS` key is owed.

Read out of the name link behind her place in days.pravoslavie.ru's line for 27 июня ст. ст., «Иоанна Мироносица» (name page 2515). The calendar's own nominative is name and epithet with no rank word in it; the line itself, «Прав. Иоанны мироносицы (I).», gives both in the genitive.

feast.note: The same menologion day this folder’s Romanian, Greek and Serbian rows already carry, so there is no second day. Her life page life1404 heads «Дни памяти: 13 апреля , 27 июня»; 13 апреля is ten weeks earlier and is not the style conversion, the day page for it was not read, and nothing is claimed about it here beyond that the calendar lists it. The line grades her «Прав.», righteous, and dates her «(I)», the first century, which this folder records in no field, having none. The day page prints no hymn under her name.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 27 июня ст. ст. — «Прав. Иоанны мироносицы (I).»

feast.note: doxologia.ro's life adds that the Church keeps her also on the Sunday of the Myrrhbearers, which is a Pascha offset and not a fixed day; only the fixed day is recorded here.

attestations.note: The day’s third entry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. The Julian 27 June is the same menologion number this folder’s Romanian and Greek rows carry, so there is no second day and no §4 note is owed; the Russian row stays `undocumented`. **A RANK WORD IN THE HEADING FOR WHICH THIS CORPUS HAS NO TYPE AT ALL, AND `types` STAYS NULL.** „Света Јоана Мироносица“ gives Света, which is not a rank, and Мироносица, myrrh-bearer — **which is a rank word, is in the heading, and therefore ought by the standing rule to be written; and it cannot be.** `grep -ho '"types": \[[^]]*\]' saints/*/saint.json` returns **no myrrh-bearer type anywhere in the corpus**, and the vocabulary this wave may write into a folder has no word for it: not `righteous`, not `virgin`, not `monastic`, none of which the heading says. A new type is a code commit and is out of scope, so **nothing is written and it is said here instead**, which is what the brief tells a reader to do when nothing fits. This folder’s `types` is **null** before and after, and it was null before this reading too — the Romanian and Greek lines gave it nothing either, and `eutropius-companion-of-tigrius` is the precedent the upgrade script already carries for a folder with no types at all. **AUTHOR: this is the first entry of the wave whose heading rank the vocabulary cannot express.** **`dates` STAYS NULL.** „Упокојила се мирно.“, she reposed peacefully, is the whole of what the entry says about her end: no year, no age, no reign. „Тек у време Константина Великог та је глава обретена.“ puts the finding of the Forerunner’s head тек у време Константина Великог, only in the time of Constantine the Great — **an emperor is no source for a year, a finding of relics is not a death, and the finding is not even hers.** Nothing is written. **AND THAT NAME IS KEPT OUT OF THE LIFE ON PURPOSE.** `constantine-the-great` is a folder whose display name is the bare string «Constantine the Great», three words, which `usableName` accepts, so the cross-linker matches it in prose and `related-floor.test.mjs` demands a row both ways — and the gate’s own exclusion list already holds, as one of its two singletons, the case of **an emperor named to date a life**, which is exactly this. Measured with `.tmp/sr-prosechk.mjs` before the paragraph was drafted, the name is on this row and not in the life, and **nothing was added to `scripts/related-floor-exclusions.json`**. **THE ROW THIS ENTRY IS ENTIRELY ABOUT, AND THE RECIPROCAL IT WAS MISSING.** „Када Ирод посече Јована Крститеља, он му баци главу на нечисто место.“ and „Јоана узе главу Крститељеву и погребе је чесно на Јелеонској гори, на имању Иродову.“ — when Herod beheaded John the Baptist he threw the head into an unclean place, and Joanna took the Forerunner’s head and buried it honourably on the Mount of Olives, on Herod’s own estate. **The whole of what this book knows about her is that act**, which makes the relation this entry’s own reading rather than an inference. `john-the-baptist` was already in this folder’s `related` — and **the reciprocal was missing**, that folder’s `related` being null outright. It is added here, both ways now, on the strength of this entry: a burial of the relics by a named woman is her story and his. „Жена Хузе, дворјанина Иродова.“ makes her the wife of Chuza, Herod’s courtier, which is the «wife of Chuza» the display name already carries; **Chuza takes no row**, `grep` returning no folder of that name, and Herod takes none either. `mary-magdalene` is `related` here already, this book does not name her, and the row is untouched. „Света Јоана спомиње се као присутна и при страдању и при васкрсењу Господа.“ has her remembered as present both at the Lord’s passion and at His resurrection, which is the one thing this book adds about her beyond the burial. No `locations`: the Mount of Olives is named in a clause. No `office`. **RULING 3 ON THE DAY’S SECOND ENTRY, AND THE INSTRUMENT HANDS BACK THE WRONG MAN.** „Свети Севир, презвитер“ is a person and gets no folder from this reader. „Живео у средњој Италији.“ and „Муж необичне светости.“ — he lived in central Italy, a man of unusual holiness; „Једном позван беше да исповеди и причести самртника, но он задоцни радећи у винограду.“ has him called to shrive and communicate a dying man and come late because he was working in his vineyard, „Сав устрашен, као да је он убица онога човека, поче горко плакати над мртвацем.“ has him weep bitterly over the corpse as though he were the man’s murderer, „И по његовој усрдној молитви Бог оживе мртваца.“ has God raise the dead man at his earnest prayer, and „Осмога дана онај човек поново умре.“ has that man die again on the eighth day after being shriven and communicated and made ready for a Christian parting. **`foldchk.py` on «Севир» returns a holder** — `severus-of-philippopolis`, in `ru` — **and he is not this man**: a martyr of Philippopolis with an attested 304 and a `related` row to a centurion, kept on 20 August by three calendars. `ls saints | grep -iE '^sever'` returns nine folders and the five plausible ones are all somebody else: `severus-3-november` and `severus-the-martyr-8-september` are bare-line Greek martyrs, `severus-companion-of-leucius` is named only as another man’s companion, and `severinus-of-noricum` is a monk and preacher of Noricum kept on 8 January. **An identification off a bare forename is not an identification**, and the exact-string match is the sharpest illustration of that this wave has produced: the instrument answers about a string and the reading is about a man. Named here, no folder, no row, and his name is kept out of every life on this day. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. THE VERSE IS NOT USED. The ПЕСМА for 27 June is on the first entry and its charity, and nothing on the presbyter or the myrrh-bearer. It is Bishop Nikolai’s own and §3 of this wave’s brief puts it in no field and in no life. **It was read before this was written**, after the Julian 26 June, where a guess about which entry the verse treated was wrong and had to be corrected out of a batch already applied.
